subject: Stan crashes after first chain completes

messages.author: b17f4d0880547804
messages.subject: Stan crashes after first chain completes
parts:
Hi everyone,
I'm working with a relatively simple model being applied to a large amount of data (180,000 observations). I need to extract the summary estimates of both true_dbh1 and true_dbh2 (i.e. 180,000 x 2 estimates).
The model works fine on subsets of data (e.g. 20,000 observations). But when I apply it to the entire dataset it seems to crash after the first chain completes.
I thought this may be due to it maxing out the RAM. But throughout it's entire run it was using ~ 3gb (1gb per chain) out of a possible 16 gb of RAM.
The model takes about 7 hours to run so it's difficult to diagnose the problem.
I'm using rstan 2.6 and mclapply to run the chains in parallel via the terminal.
Attached is the console crash report, data and model.

Any advice would be greatly appreciated!



  stan_data <- list(
    n_obs = nrow(data),
    census_length = data$census_interval,
    obs_dbh1 = data$dbh_prev,
    obs_dbh2 = data$dbh)
  
  true_dbh_model <-'
    data {
      int<lower=1> n_obs;
      vector[n_obs] census_length;
      vector[n_obs] obs_dbh1;
      vector[n_obs] obs_dbh2;
    }
  
  parameters {
    real<lower=0> true_dbh1[n_obs];
    real log_mu_true_dbh1;
    real<lower=0> log_sigma_true_dbh1;
    real<lower=0> dbh_increment[n_obs];
  }
  
  model {
    real true_dbh2[n_obs];
    
    for (i in 1:n_obs) {
      // Calculating true growth for fitted data
      true_dbh2[i] <- true_dbh1[i] + (dbh_increment[i] * census_length[i]);
    }
    
    // Observation error
    obs_dbh1 ~ normal(true_dbh1, 0.75);
    obs_dbh2 ~ normal(true_dbh2, 0.75);
    
    // Priors
    log_mu_true_dbh1 ~ normal(0,2.5);
    log_sigma_true_dbh1 ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
    true_dbh1 ~ lognormal(log_mu_true_dbh1, log_sigma_true_dbh1);
    dbh_increment ~ lognormal(0,1);
  }
  
  generated quantities {
    real true_dbh2[n_obs];
    
    for (i in 1:n_obs) {
      // recalculating true growth for fitted data
      true_dbh2[i] <- true_dbh1[i] + (dbh_increment[i] * census_length[i]);
    }
  }'
  
  fit <- sflist2stanfit(mclapply(1:3, mc.cores=3,
                                 function(i) {
                                   stan(model_code = true_dbh_model, 
                                        data= stan_data,
                                        pars = c("log_mu_true_dbh1","log_sigma_true_dbh1",
                                                 "true_dbh1","true_dbh2"), 
                                        chains = 1,
                                        chain_id = i,
                                        iter = 1000, 
                                        control=list(stepsize=0.05, adapt_delta=0.9),
                                        refresh=1,
                                        thin=5) 
                                   }))

Sorry about that --- it's rude of Stan to crash R.

Is there a way to run RStan so that it only outputs to
file and doesn't save internally? If so, that would be
an even better alternative that would keep you in R.

Otherwise, I'd suggest running large jobs in CmdStan. It's
easy to export the data from RStan and once you have
RStan installed, you have all the pieces on your machine
you need to run CmdStan. Then you can read the data back into
RStan in one go for analysis and it shouldn't have a problem with
sizing.

- Bob

Thanks Krzysztof & Bob, I'm not aware of a way to make stan save the output externally rather than internally.

But then I kept running into this issue. So I decided to run rstan by itself. Still no cigar. ;)

I did look into specifying a sample_file in the stan function. But I couldn't get it to work.. possibly because I wasn't specifying it correctly.
I did something like...

Though I don't think this helps as stan still saves things internally.

I'll look into CmdStan. Hopefully, it's fairly straightforward ;). Though Ideally I'd like to stay within Rstan as this model is part of a broader project that is pretty much all R based.

On Tuesday, July 14, 2015 at 12:31:04 AM UTC-4, James Camac wrote:
I didn't know get_posterior_means() would also give you the estimates of unmonitored parameters!
I'll give it a try! Though is there a way to calculate the Rhats/effective sample sizes associated with these posteriors? Just to make sure they have adequately converged?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Stan crashes after first chain completes
parts:
[a bit of x-over with stan-dev]

R-hat's possible to calculate as you go using sufficient
stat accumulators, but split R-hat's trickier unless you know
the chain length ahead of time because otherwise you need
a lot of buffering to anticipate the split.

n_eff isn't possible because it requires the whole chain
for autocorrelations (some approximation would probalby
be possible, with same split-chain issues as R-hat).

The quantiles are also tough --- you need q% of the samples to
properly compute a q% quantile at each end.

We'd probably want to generalize to the ragged version,
which we haven't decided how to do yet (weight by chain, weight
by draw, or somewhere in between), but either way will
reduce to the usual method in the non-ragged case.

-Bob
